$comment: The gauntlet: what 'the index works' actually means, in a file rather than in someone's memory. `rustgraph.py selftest` runs it and exits non-zero on any mismatch, and lint-index runs that -- which is also the only thing in CI that executes any Python at all. Expectations are deliberately about the TOP result, since that is what an agent acts on. When the README or the crates.io dump legitimately changes an answer, update the expectation in the same commit and say why.

queries.note: The list says Encoding and never serialization; this passes only via category term profiles.
Regression guard: clap's 1.1B downloads used to win this on fame alone.
README never says REST. Passes only via crates.io keywords; was NO ANCHOR before them.
Reached through the crates.io keyword 'orm', not the category name.
Was right by accident via AI/Genetic algorithms; keywords make it right via Concurrency.
Reached by keyword rarity: 'scraping' belongs to one crate here, while 'web' belongs to forty.
Named-crate lookup. Returned Kiss3d while the exact-name bonus was wired to the README-only crate_name field.
Named-crate lookup where the name is moderately common in corpus text.
Changed from bevy deliberately when POP_WEIGHT dropped: ggez is a dedicated 2D framework and bevy, a general engine, is now second. A ranking trade, not a data change.
Capability phrasing containing a crate name. The dead `websocket` crate is outdownloaded 110x by tungstenite in its own category, which is what disqualifies its name match.
Adoption used to beat intent here: core-foundation, a macOS-only binding with 411M downloads, outranked the crate described as a cross-platform GUI library.
Was returning shlex with rand at sixth.

queries.q: read a config file and validate it

queries.note: Paraphrase of a tuned query. Returned a line-editing crate until plural folding let structopt's 'command line argument' match 'arguments'.
Plural paraphrase of 'date and time'; was returning cargo-update.

no_anchor.note: Must report no category match rather than dressing a guess as a ranking.

confidence.note: Gibberish must not be answered confidently.
One token hits the obscure crate `quantum`; a name match on part of a query is not confidence in the query.

confidence.q: garbage collection tuning for the JVM heap
confidence.note: Out of scope for a Rust list.
Confident via exact crate name rather than category.

confidence.q: I want to hash passwords securely
confidence.note: Top hit is an UNVERIFIED guess; a guessed crate name must never carry high confidence, least of all for a security question.
Only 'HTTP' survives tokenising. Coverage is measured in characters so this cannot claim 100%.

affinity.note: gRPC codegen; the highest-lift pair in the index and a check that lift is not just counting popularity.

runtime.note: Optional in Cargo.toml but inside the default closure; a plain optional flag would call this a free choice.
Genuinely runtime-agnostic: neither runtime is in its default closure.

features.note: Implicit only: chrono's serde feature exists because it optionally depends on serde, which this list does not carry.

examples.note: clap's crates.io README defers to docs.rs. Guarded so the absence stays honest rather than becoming a silent regression.
